        "domain": "component",
        "name": "VisuallyHidden",
        "package": "@astryxdesign/core",
        "score": 90,
        "reason": "keyword \"accessibility\"",
        "description": "Renders content in the accessibility tree while hiding it visually. Use for accessible names on icon-only controls, aria-live announcement regions, and supplementary screen-reader context. Deliberately has no styling props; the whole point is to stay invisible. `xstyle` is still accepted and ignored, only so code written against 0.7.2 keeps compiling; a planned minor removes it.",
        "import": "@astryxdesign/core/VisuallyHidden",
        "command": "astryx component VisuallyHidden"
      },
      {
        "domain": "hook",
        "name": "useAnnounce",
        "package": "@astryxdesign/core",
        "score": 90,
        "reason": "keyword \"accessibility\"",
        "description": "Imperatively announces a message to screen readers through a visually-hidden live region. Use it for state that is only conveyed visually; search result counts, \"no results\", loading and saved confirmations, validation errors (WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages). The polite and assertive regions are created empty on first use and stay mounted, which is what makes announcements reliable: most screen readers ignore a live region that is inserted together with its content. Each message is cleared a couple of seconds after it is announced so stale status does not linger in the accessibility tree. A message is delivered where its caller is: from inside an open Astryx modal it goes to a region inside that modal and is heard there with no change to the calling code; a message sent just as the modal is dismissed is delivered through whatever is exposed afterwards rather than lost. A call made outside the modal, even by the component that renders it, uses the page-body region.",
        "import": "@astryxdesign/core/hooks",
        "command": "astryx hook useAnnounce"
      },
      {
        "domain": "hook",
        "name": "useCombobox",
        "package": "@astryxdesign/core",
        "score": 90,
        "reason": "keyword \"accessibility\"",
        "description": "Tracks the active option of a single-select combobox and handles its keys, while DOM focus stays on the control. It powers Selector and CommandPalette; use it to build a combobox those components do not cover, including one over a single-line text field you render yourself, such as a search field whose results replace a page section, or an “add people” field in a dialog. It renders nothing: you render the field, the listbox and the options, and spread `getFieldProps`, `getListboxProps` and `getOptionProps` onto them, or wire `role`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` and `aria-activedescendant` yourself from `onKeyDown` and `getItemId` for a control such as a button.",
        "import": "@astryxdesign/core/Selector",
        "command": "astryx hook useCombobox"
      },
      {
        "domain": "hook",
        "name": "useFocusTrap",
        "package": "@astryxdesign/core",
        "score": 90,
        "reason": "keyword \"accessibility\"",
        "description": "Traps focus within a container element following the WAI-ARIA dialog focus trap pattern. Listens to focus events on the document and redirects focus back into the container if a Tab from inside it moves focus out. Handles both Tab and Shift+Tab wrapping. A Tab pressed while focus is outside the container is left to the page, so an open non-modal surface never takes over the focus order of the page. When the trap deactivates or unmounts, focus is restored to the element that was focused before activation, unless focus was already moved elsewhere or never entered the trap (so popups that keep focus on their trigger, like comboboxes, are unaffected). Mouse clicks outside the container are not intercepted; use a light-dismiss handler for that.",
        "import": "@astryxdesign/core/hooks",
        "command": "astryx hook useFocusTrap"
      },
      {
        "domain": "hook",
        "name": "useIndicatorFocusRing",
        "package": "@astryxdesign/core",
        "score": 90,
        "reason": "keyword \"accessibility\"",
        "description": "Draws the standard focus ring on the indicator of a control whose real input is visually hidden; a checkbox or radio focuses an opacity-0 input, so the ring has to appear on the picture beside it. The ring is painted imperatively on the indicator's own element, which is the only element whose border-radius can shape it, and only on :focus-visible, so pointer clicks stay quiet. Owning it here means a theme-supplied indicator cannot ship a control with no visible focus (WCAG 2.4.7) by ignoring a prop.",
        "import": "@astryxdesign/core/hooks",
        "command": "astryx hook useIndicatorFocusRing"
      },
      {
        "domain": "hook",
        "name": "useInputStatusIcon",
        "package": "@astryxdesign/core",
        "score": 90,
        "reason": "keyword \"accessibility\"",
        "description": "Builds the on-field status affordance for a bordered input and its accessibility wiring, so every input in the family behaves the same for a given status. The attached variant renders a plain glyph and leaves the text to the message box; the detached variant renders nothing here, because the message box already carries its own icon; the tooltip variant renders a real focusable button whose tooltip is reachable by keyboard, pointer, touch and assistive tech. Use it when building a bordered input, not for field-level messaging.",
        "import": "@astryxdesign/core/hooks",
        "command": "astryx hook useInputStatusIcon"
      }
